text: This is a bicycle repair shop. Not a startup. A shop on a real street.
It has no API team. But it publishes its front desk as an agent network: one JSON file, and any assistant can talk to it.
I will ask it something a customer would actually ask.
Three agents run, in my browser. The front desk, the workshop lead, the parts desk. And when the workshop lead names a part, the page points at it.
The price comes from the shop's own book. Forty pounds fifty in labour, plus the parts. Not from the model.
Two lines are not on the shelf, so it asks a different origin for stock. I have to allow that. My phone number stays in this tab. The trade counter gets the shop's account number, and nothing else.
Thursday at five thirty. Booking is a write, so I confirm it, and I get a receipt with an outcome. Confirmed. Not just the request returned.
Everything the specification asks a runtime to do, this page can be made to show. Seven checks, including the four that must fail.
The network is data. The runtime is mine. And the key, if there is one, never leaves this tab.
One JSON. Any assistant. The visitor's browser does the work. Saddle and Spoke. A shop that answers your agent.
